question: For which of the following rivers does the longitude reading decrease, as it moves along its course?
solution:
**The correct answer is 'Narmada'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada:**

 
 
• The Narmada river originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows westward across central India towards the Arabian Sea, ultimately emptying into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• As the Narmada moves along its course, its longitude readings decrease because it flows from east to west.
 
• This east-to-west flow is relatively unique among major rivers in India, which typically flow from north to south or west to east.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaveri:**

 
 
• The Kaveri river originates in the Western Ghats and flows predominantly eastward before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Hence, its longitude readings increase as it moves along its course.
 
 
 
• **Ganga:**
 
 
• The Ganga river originates in the Himalayas and also flows generally eastward towards the Bay of Bengal.
 
• As with the Kaveri, its longitude readings increase towards the end of its course.
 
 
 
• **Godavari:**
 
 
• The Godavari river originates in the central part of India and flows eastward, making its way to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Similar to the Kaveri and Ganga, the longitude readings of the Godavari increase as it progresses along its course.
